newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares fall in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares fall in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares fell on Thursday on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) a day after the company made a $77-million issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs).
A shares fell to $113.625 from Wednesday's $114.25 and B shares fell to $117 from $117.625. Turnover was 11,408 shares from 16,427 on Wednesday and value was $1,310,817.625 from $1,893,834.

The GDRs, each of which nominally represents one-tenth of an A share, were last quoted at $11.6 on the London Stock Exchange Automated Quotation system (SEAQ). They allow non-Arabs access to the market in Solidere for the first time.

"Trading in the GDRs was very quiet today mainly because U.S. markets are closed for Thanksgiving holiday," Michel Aramouni, head of treasury and capital markets at Beirut's Banque Audi, told Reuters.
There was no trade in the four other companies listed on BSE: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs,Eternit, and Uniceramic.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.44 percent to 972.55.
